summary: Stephen Chin frames context engineering as a discipline that moves beyond one-shot prompt engineering toward dynamically curating and structuring information fed to AI models. Models have huge context windows but poor attention focus, leading to hallucinations and unreliable outputs. Context engineering encompasses prompt engineering, RAG, memory (short-term and long-term), and structured output formatting. Short-term memory holds current task information, compressed and ranked by relevance, while long-term memory captures episodic, semantic, and procedural knowledge from past interactions. Knowledge graphs provide structured representations of facts, relationships, and properties—including embeddings—that both humans and LLMs can read, serving as digital twins of organizations and supply chains. GraphRAG extends standard RAG by querying a knowledge graph for relevant relational and community context, yielding more domain-specific, factual, and explainable results. Chin demonstrates the LLM Knowledge Graph Builder ingesting supply chain and VEX security documents into a Neo4j graph, then querying via a two-pass vector-lookup and related-node expansion. A second demo hooks Claude Code to a Neo4j MCP server, letting the agent retrieve the graph schema, fire Cypher queries, and pull text chunks for far more detailed vulnerability reports. Graph memory supports multi-hop queries combining people, events, and temporal context—use cases where standard vector RAG falls short. Chin also covers explicit retrieval queries, text-to-Cypher generation, and agentic graph traversal as progressively richer retrieval strategies. Knowledge graphs further enable role-based access control overlays and explainable AI through visualization of conversation flows and agent reasoning. To close, Chin directs attendees to three free resources for continued learning: Graph Academy for hands-on courses on Cypher and GraphRAG in Python and TypeScript, the Nodes AI 2026 virtual conference with AI-focused sessions and an open call for proposals, and graphrag.com for cutting-edge research, how-to guides, and conceptual information on implementing GraphRAG across problem domains.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Context Engineering Motivation
sections.summary: Chin introduces himself and frames context engineering as an evolution from prompt engineering, emphasizing dynamic context curation, domain relevance, and signal-over-noise in model inputs.

sections.title: Scope of Context Engineering
sections.summary: Defines context engineering as encompassing prompt engineering, RAG, state and history (memory), and structured output for integration with tools and applications.

sections.title: Memory: Short-Term and Long-Term
sections.summary: Details short-term memory (current task context, compression, tool result integration) and long-term memory (episodic, semantic, procedural), emphasizing relevance ranking and noise reduction to avoid hallucinations.

sections.title: Knowledge Graphs as Structured Context
sections.summary: Introduces knowledge graphs with nodes, relationships, and properties including embeddings; explains their readability for humans and LLMs and utility as digital twins of organizations.

sections.title: GraphRAG and Explainable AI
sections.summary: Defines GraphRAG as retrieval pipelines using knowledge graphs, explaining benefits over vector similarity search: relational context, domain facts, explainability, role-based access, and agent performance analysis.

sections.title: Demo Announcement
sections.summary: Announces a GraphRAG demo using the LLM Knowledge Graph Builder, already set up but not yet shown in this section.

sections.title: LLM Knowledge Graph Builder Demo: Supply Chain and VEX Documents
sections.summary: Chin demonstrates the open-source LLM Knowledge Graph Builder uploading supply chain and VEX security documents into a Neo4j Aura instance. The LLM ingests documents into a knowledge graph of nodes and relationships. A two-pass query performs vector similarity lookup then expands related nodes as context. Asking about a non-referenced Jasper library yields no response; asking about Jackson (even with a typo) returns detailed vulnerability, version, and fix information grounded in the graph.

sections.title: Graph Memory and Multi-Hop Retrieval
sections.summary: Introduces graph memory retrieval using an open-source MCP server. Graph data science algorithms—community detection, KNN, PageRank—bubble up relevant context for short-term or long-term memory. Graph memory captures entities and relationships with properties like text, embeddings, time, and location, enabling semantic vector search plus graph algorithms. A multi-hop example retrieves two presenters, an event, and temporal context for a presentation update query, illustrating where graph RAG outperforms single-shot vector RAG.

sections.title: Progressive Graph Retrieval Strategies and Claude Code MCP Demo
sections.summary: Covers explicit pre-planned retrieval queries, text-to-Cypher generation via schema fine-tuning, and agentic iterative graph traversal. A second demo connects Claude Code to a Neo4j MCP server; the agent retrieves the graph schema, fires multiple Cypher queries, and pulls text chunks to produce a detailed vulnerability report with CVE number, attack type, severity, remediation versions, and advisory information—far richer than the earlier fast vector lookup.

sections.title: Learning Resources and Closing
sections.summary: Chin points to three free resources for continued learning: Graph Academy for hands-on Cypher and GraphRAG courses with Python and TypeScript examples plus upcoming advanced GraphRAG courses; Nodes AI 2026, a free online virtual conference focused on AI with an open CFP following a 13,000-registrant Nodes conference; and graphrag.com, a community site with cutting-edge research, how-to guides, and conceptual information for implementing GraphRAG across problem domains. He closes by thanking attendees and encouraging them to use graphs to connect the dots in context engineering.

demonstrations: LLM Knowledge Graph Builder ingesting supply chain and VEX security documents into a Neo4j graph, querying Jackson vulnerability via two-pass vector lookup and related-node expansion
Claude Code connected to Neo4j MCP server performing multi-step Cypher queries for detailed vulnerability remediation information
Graph memory example retrieving a multi-hop query combining presenter, colleague, event, and temporal context for presentation update
limitations: Fast vector-similarity GraphRAG lookup gives limited detail compared to slower agentic multi-step traversal
Standard vector RAG is sufficient only for single-shot or single-similarity-search use cases; graph RAG adds value when relationships span two or more hops
